13:   alias Dhc.Notifications
14:   alias Dhc.Repo
15: 
16:   @type invite_data :: map()
17:   @type invite_result :: map()
18: 
19:   @spec invitation_id_for_issue_key(String.t()) :: {:ok, Ecto.UUID.t()} | :not_found
20:   def invitation_id_for_issue_key(issue_key) when is_binary(issue_key) do
21:     from(i in Invitation,
22:       where: fragment("?->>'issue_key'", i.metadata) == ^issue_key,
23:       select: i.id
24:     )
25:     |> Repo.one()
26:     |> case do
27:       nil -> :not_found
28:       invitation_id -> {:ok, invitation_id}
29:     end
30:   end
31: 
32:   @doc """
33:   Inserts a pending Invitation and returns its ID.
34: 
35:   Mints a fresh Phoenix UUID for `prospective_principal_id` (the eventual Principal id). Under
36:   ALE-162 this is not an `auth.users` id; the auth.users FK was dropped and
37:   acceptance will create the Principal with this id.
38:   """
39:   @spec insert_pending_invitation(invite_data(), String.t() | nil, String.t() | nil) ::
40:           {:ok, Ecto.UUID.t()} | {:error, term()}
41:   def insert_pending_invitation(invite_data, waitlist_id, created_by_id) do
42:     invitation = %Invitation{
43:       id: Ecto.UUID.generate(),
44:       email: invite_data["email"],
45:       prospective_principal_id: Ecto.UUID.generate(),
46:       waitlist_id: waitlist_id,
47:       status: "pending",
48:       expires_at: DateTime.utc_now() |> DateTime.add(7, :day) |> DateTime.truncate(:second),
49:       created_by_principal_id: created_by_id,
50:       invitation_type: Map.get(invite_data, "invitationType", "admin"),
51:       pricing_tier: Map.get(invite_data, "pricingTier", "standard"),
52:       metadata: Map.get(invite_data, "metadata"),
53:       first_name: invite_data["firstName"],
54:       last_name: invite_data["lastName"],
55:       phone_number: invite_data["phoneNumber"],
56:       date_of_birth: parse_date(invite_data["dateOfBirth"])
57:     }
58: 
59:     case Repo.insert(invitation) do
60:       {:ok, invitation} -> {:ok, invitation.id}
61:       {:error, reason} -> {:error, reason}
62:     end
63:   rescue
64:     error in [Ecto.ConstraintError, Postgrex.Error] -> {:error, error}
65:   end
66: 
67:   @doc """
68:   Writes one Invitation processing-log entry over `results`.
69:   `Dhc.Onboarding` writes one entry per issued or refused invite.
70:   """
71:   @spec store_processing_results([invite_result()], String.t()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
72:   def store_processing_results(results, created_by_id) when is_list(results) do
73:     success_count = Enum.count(results, & &1.success)
74:     failure_count = length(results) - success_count
75: 
76:     log = %ProcessingLog{
77:       principal_id: created_by_id,
78:       total_count: length(results),
79:       success_count: success_count,
80:       failure_count: failure_count,
81:       results: %{"items" => results},
82:       created_at: DateTime.utc_now() |> DateTime.truncate(:second)
83:     }
84: 
85:     case Repo.insert(log) do
86:       {:ok, _log} -> :ok
87:       {:error, reason} -> {:error, {:processing_log, reason}}
88:     end
89:   rescue
90:     error in [Ecto.ConstraintError, Postgrex.Error] -> {:error, {:processing_log, error}}
91:   end
92: 
93:   @doc """
94:   Writes one processing-log entry for a refused invite (issue or re-arm),
95:   outside the rolled-back transaction so the entry survives.
96:   """
97:   @spec store_refusal(String.t() | nil, term(), String.t()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
98:   def store_refusal(email, reason, created_by_id) do
99:     store_processing_results(
100:       [%{email: email || "unknown", success: false, error: inspect(reason)}],
101:       created_by_id
102:     )
103:   end
104: 
105:   @doc """
106:   Creates the admin Notification summarising a bulk Invitation run.
107:   """
108:   @spec create_processing_notification([invite_result()], String.t()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
109:   def create_processing_notification(results, created_by_id) when is_list(results) do
110:     success_count = Enum.count(results, & &1.success)
111:     failure_count = length(results) - success_count
112: 
113:     body =
114:       if failure_count == 0 do
115:         "Successfully processed #{success_count} invitations out of #{length(results)}"
116:       else
117:         "Successfully processed #{success_count} invitations out of #{length(results)}, failed to process #{failure_count} invitations"
118:       end
119: 
120:     case Notifications.create(created_by_id, body) do
121:       :ok -> :ok
122:       {:error, reason} -> {:error, {:notification, reason}}
123:     end
124:   end
125: 
126:   @doc """
127:   Normalises supported date shapes into the date string accepted by Postgres.
128:   """
129:   @spec date_string(Date.t() | DateTime.t() | String.t() | term()) :: String.t()
130:   def date_string(%Date{} = date), do: Date.to_iso8601(date)
131:   def date_string(%DateTime{} = date_time), do: DateTime.to_date(date_time) |> Date.to_iso8601()
132: 
133:   def date_string(value) when is_binary(value) do
134:     value
135:     |> String.split("T")
136:     |> List.first()
137:   end
138: 
139:   def date_string(value), do: to_string(value)
140: 
141:   defp parse_date(%Date{} = date), do: date
142:   defp parse_date(%DateTime{} = date_time), do: DateTime.to_date(date_time)
143: 
144:   defp parse_date(value) when is_binary(value) and value != "" do
145:     value
146:     |> String.split("T")
147:     |> List.first()
148:     |> Date.from_iso8601!()
149:   end
150: 
151:   defp parse_date(_value), do: nil
152: end

This is a web application written using the Phoenix web framework.

## Project guidelines

- Use `mix precommit` when you are done and fix pending issues. Its alias must keep `hex.audit` first because dependency-provided tasks unload archived Hex tasks from the current Mix process; it then runs Credo, `reach.check --arch`, compilation, formatting, and tests.
- Production Docker tool versions still come from root `.mise.toml`, projected by `tools/phoenix-toolchain-config.sh`. Keep projection in its separate `toolchain-config` stage and copy only `beam.toml`/`runtime.toml` into install stages; projecting inside an install stage would still rebuild OTP after unrelated mise edits.
- Legacy end times have one approved deployment exception: the ALE-431 data migration fills missing values (historical rows included) with start + six civil hours, preserving explicit ends and leaving starts at/after 18:00 unknown. Operational backfills still use `execute/3`'s authorized `backfill_end_time` command before the Dublin start instant; known-time corrections use reschedule. Neither backfill changes deadlines or attendance policy; see `docs/workshop-calendar.md`.
- Workshop Calendar source changes call `Dhc.WorkshopCalendar.record_change/2` or `record_deleted/2` inside their existing transaction; integration rows retain identity and cleanup after source deletion, and an absent Google event is not proof that a timed-out insert cannot arrive later. Read `docs/workshop-calendar.md` before changing reconciliation or enabling sends.
- Regular Workshop Calendar Invitations capture the saved participant address with `confirm_place/4` in the new-confirmation branch of PaymentCommands or the source-locked launch backfill; its legacy Checkout payer fallback is not a participant address. One Google guest can serve several logical places, so removing one binding preserves another active binding's guest and RSVP; see the participant protocol in `docs/workshop-calendar.md`.
- Beginners' Workshop Calendar projections keep early-finalised workshops scheduled: only the explicit scheduled end stops publication and repair, not attendance finalisation. Unknown legacy ends remain `nil`; schedule/backfill commands re-arm that data failure through the shared Calendar intent, never by guessing a duration.
- Beginners' Workshop Calendar Invitations bind the locked Waitlist email when an Intake becomes paid (Stripe completion or credit confirmation in `IntakeCommands`, shared by person and staff) or through the source-locked launch backfill; held credit and confirmation replays create no entitlement. Explicit lost-place Settlement rows own `:remove_calendar_place`. `calendar_place_ids/1` reads confirmation history, not current attendance state: keep attendance corrections (including no-show → deferred) removal-free. See `docs/workshop-calendar.md` for the shared participant protocol.
- Person deletion records `WorkshopCalendar.forget_places/2` before Intake anonymisation, inside `Commands.People`'s existing locked transaction. Keep its address-free binding tombstones: cleanup scrubs addresses only after fenced Google acknowledgment, including after event end; place cancellation alone does not erase them. See `docs/workshop-calendar.md` for privacy recovery and external-copy limits.
- Calendar launch (ALE-437) is `mix dhc.workshop_calendar.preview` then explicit `activate isolated|production`, matching `WORKSHOP_CALENDAR_ENVIRONMENT`; only target-bound database activation enables non-test sending. Preview loads `app.config` and a temporary Repo, never `app.start`, which would wake workers. Keep source materialization inside PaymentCommands/Commands.CalendarLaunch and existing bindings immutable. The narrowed scope keeps automatic sync/retries but claims terminal failure episodes durably before best-effort post-commit Sentry capture, not dashboard Notifications; pause/resume and manual recipient-correction APIs are removed. See `docs/workshop-calendar.md`.
- Training Calendar sharing belongs to `Dhc.TrainingCalendar`, with its own ACL-only OAuth credential and grant ledger; keep it separate from Workshop Calendar's event-only authorization. Read `docs/training-calendar.md` before changing sharing ownership, the Dublin-midnight Cron gate, or enablement.
- Waitlist entry positions are numbered across the full selected standing before search or cursor filtering; `totalCount` still counts only search matches. Keep search outside `positioned_entries_query/1`'s subquery in `Dhc.Waitlist`.
- Waitlist `last_contacted` means the latest queued email, not confirmed delivery. `IntakeEmails.deliver/5` advances it monotonically through `Dhc.Waitlist.record_contact/2` after queueing and logging; every emailing command must lock the recipient's Waitlist entry before Intake/payment rows, including reschedule and follow-up passes.
- Keep Bandit at `~> 1.14` or newer within the compatible minor line; 1.12.5 fixes CVE-2026-74836/75484 and 1.14.0 fixes the October-2026 HTTP/2 and WebSocket set (CVE-2026-108525, -109584, -110314, -110499, -111101, -111103, -113436, -114213, -114216, -115269). plug_crypto must stay at `~> 2.2.1` (CVE-2026-105963: guard failures leaked the secret key base into logs).
- Run `mix credo --all` from `apps/phoenix` for static analysis; the project configuration also enables `ExSlop`
- Reach enforces module boundaries in `.reach.exs`: web→Repo only via `DhcWeb.Plugs.MagicLinkRateLimit`, Stripe only via `Dhc.Stripe.Operations.*` (never `Dhc.Stripe.Client.request/1`), Nostrum only inside `Dhc.Discord.*`, Req as the only HTTP client, no `IO.puts` outside Mix tasks/`Dhc.Release`. New findings fail the build; baseline known transitional findings with `MIX_ENV=dev mix reach.check --arch --write-baseline .reach-baseline.json`
- **Stripe test seam (ALE-342)**: every Stripe HTTP call goes through `Dhc.Stripe.Client` (via `Dhc.Stripe.Operations.*`), which merges `:stripe_req_options`; tests run it against `plug: {Req.Test, Dhc.Stripe}`. Stub Stripe HTTP with `Dhc.StripeHTTPStub` (`stub/3`, `expect/4`, `form/1`, `json/3`) — no Bypass, and tests never `put_env` `:stripe_api_url`, `:stripe_secret_key` or `:stripe_req_options`. Workshop tests pick one of three seams: `Dhc.StripeHTTPStub` for a test that stubs a few Stripe routes; `DhcWeb.WorkshopStripeClient` (a whole-Stripe `Req.Test` plug, `Req.Test.stub(Dhc.Stripe, DhcWeb.WorkshopStripeClient)`) for workshop controller contract tests that should run the live adapter; and `Dhc.Workshops.StripeStub` (the `:workshop_stripe_adapter`, app-env driven) for `PaymentCommands` workflow tests whose Stripe call runs outside the test's `$callers` tree (unboxed concurrency tasks) or must be paused. The one exception: real-Stripe `:integration` suites `put_env` a real `:stripe_secret_key` and reset `:stripe_req_options` to `[]` in setup (and restore both on exit); no other test changes Stripe config. Stubs reach Tasks/inline jobs via `$callers`; other processes need `Req.Test.allow/3`. Shared subscription-payment decoding lives in `Dhc.Stripe.SubscriptionPayment` and the one retry rule in `Dhc.Stripe.Failure.retryable?/1`; see "Stubbing Stripe" in `docs/agents/notes.md`.
- Keep generated Stripe modules under `lib/dhc/stripe/generated/` excluded from Credo instead of refactoring generated source
- Use the already included and available `:req` (`Req`) library for HTTP requests, **avoid** `:httpoison`, `:tesla`, and `:httpc`. Req is included by default and is the preferred HTTP client for Phoenix apps
- **Documented exception (ADR 0021)**: transactional email goes through Swoosh, whose api client is `config :swoosh, api_client: Dhc.Email.ApiClient` wrapping `Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch` over a named `{Finch, name: Swoosh.Finch}` child in `Dhc.Application`. Finch is already a production dependency, so Hackney stays out of prod. Application code outside `Dhc.Email.*` still uses Req everywhere else.
- Hackney is test-only because Testcontainers requires its 1.x Unix-socket transport. Keep it out of production and do not force Hackney 4 until Testcontainers supports Docker Unix sockets with it; the matching Hackney advisory exceptions in `mix.exs` apply only to that test dependency.
- Nostrum's REST client pulls Gun and Cowlib into production (Gun is floored at 2.7 in `mix.exs`, which resolves Cowlib 2.21 — fixed for CVE-2026-43971 and CVE-2026-43969). Limit Cowlib advisory exceptions to explicitly reviewed CVE IDs and document the relevant exposure or mitigation in `mix.exs`; keep ignoring CVE-2026-43966 only until a fixed Cowlib release ships, and keep the Hackney 4-only CVE exceptions (CVE-2026-47069/47071/47075/47076) only while Testcontainers requires Hackney 1.x.

### Phoenix v1.8 guidelines

- **Always** begin your LiveView templates with `<Layouts.app flash={@flash} ...>` which wraps all inner content
- The `MyAppWeb.Layouts` module is aliased in the `my_app_web.ex` file, so you can use it without needing to alias it again
- Anytime you run into errors with no `current_scope` assign:
  - You failed to follow the Authenticated Routes guidelines, or you failed to pass `current_scope` to `<Layouts.app>`
  - **Always** fix the `current_scope` error by moving your routes to the proper `live_session` and ensure you pass `current_scope` as needed
- Phoenix v1.8 moved the `<.flash_group>` component to the `Layouts` module. You are **forbidden** from calling `<.flash_group>` outside of the `layouts.ex` module
- Out of the box, `core_components.ex` imports an `<.icon name="hero-x-mark" class="w-5 h-5"/>` component for hero icons. **Always** use the `<.icon>` component for icons, **never** use `Heroicons` modules or similar
- **Always** use the imported `<.input>` component for form inputs from `core_components.ex` when available. `<.input>` is imported and using it will save steps and prevent errors
- If you override the default input classes (`<.input class="myclass px-2 py-1 rounded-lg">)`) class with your own values, no default classes are inherited, so your
custom classes must fully style the input


<!-- usage-rules-start -->

<!-- phoenix:elixir-start -->
## Elixir guidelines

- Elixir lists **do not support index based access via the access syntax**

  **Never do this (invalid)**:

      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      mylist[i]

  Instead, **always** use `Enum.at`, pattern matching, or `List` for index based list access, ie:

      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      Enum.at(mylist, i)

- Elixir variables are immutable, but can be rebound, so for block expressions like `if`, `case`, `cond`, etc
  you *must* bind the result of the expression to a variable if you want to use it and you CANNOT rebind the result inside the expression, ie:

      # INVALID: we are rebinding inside the `if` and the result never gets assigned
      if connected?(socket) do
        socket = assign(socket, :val, val)
      end

      # VALID: we rebind the result of the `if` to a new variable
      socket =
        if connected?(socket) do
          assign(socket, :val, val)
        end

- **Never** nest multiple modules in the same file as it can cause cyclic dependencies and compilation errors
- **Never** use map access syntax (`changeset[:field]`) on structs as they do not implement the Access behaviour by default. For regular structs, you **must** access the fields directly, such as `my_struct.field` or use higher level APIs that are available on the struct if they exist, `Ecto.Changeset.get_field/2` for changesets
- Elixir's standard library has everything necessary for date and time manipulation. Familiarize yourself with the common `Time`, `Date`, `DateTime`, and `Calendar` interfaces by accessing their documentation as necessary. The one sanctioned date/time dependency is `tz`, the IANA database behind `Dhc.ClubCalendar`'s Europe/Dublin conversions. **Never** install additional dependencies unless asked or for date/time parsing (which you can use the `date_time_parser` package)
- Don't use `String.to_atom/1` on user input (memory leak risk)
- Predicate function names should not start with `is_` and should end in a question mark. Names like `is_thing` should be reserved for guards
- Elixir's builtin OTP primitives like `DynamicSupervisor` and `Registry`, require names in the child spec, such as `{DynamicSupervisor, name: MyApp.MyDynamicSup}`, then you can use `DynamicSupervisor.start_child(MyApp.MyDynamicSup, child_spec)`
- Use `Task.async_stream(collection, callback, options)` for concurrent enumeration with back-pressure. The majority of times you will want to pass `timeout: :infinity` as option

## Mix guidelines

- Read the docs and options before using tasks (by using `mix help task_name`)
- To debug test failures, run tests in a specific file with `mix test test/my_test.exs` or run all previously failed tests with `mix test --failed`
- `mix deps.clean --all` is **almost never needed**. **Avoid** using it unless you have good reason

## Test guidelines

- **Always use `start_supervised!/1`** to start processes in tests as it guarantees cleanup between tests
- **Avoid** `Process.sleep/1` and `Process.alive?/1` in tests
  - Instead of sleeping to wait for a process to finish, **always** use `Process.monitor/1` and assert on the DOWN message:

      ref = Process.monitor(pid)
      assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :normal}

   - Instead of sleeping to synchronize before the next call, **always** use `_ = :sys.get_state/1` to ensure the process has handled prior messages
<!-- phoenix:elixir-end -->

<!-- phoenix:phoenix-start -->
## Phoenix guidelines

- Remember Phoenix router `scope` blocks include an optional alias which is prefixed for all routes within the scope. **Always** be mindful of this when creating routes within a scope to avoid duplicate module prefixes.

- You **never** need to create your own `alias` for route definitions! The `scope` provides the alias, ie:

      scope "/admin", AppWeb.Admin do
        pipe_through :browser

        live "/users", UserLive, :index
      end

  the UserLive route would point to the `AppWeb.Admin.UserLive` module

- `Phoenix.View` no longer is needed or included with Phoenix, don't use it
<!-- phoenix:phoenix-end -->

<!-- phoenix:ecto-start -->
## Ecto Guidelines

- **Always** preload Ecto associations in queries when they'll be accessed in templates, ie a message that needs to reference the `message.user.email`
- Remember `import Ecto.Query` and other supporting modules when you write `seeds.exs`
- `Ecto.Schema` fields always use the `:string` type, even for `:text`, columns, ie: `field :name, :string`
- `Ecto.Changeset.validate_number/2` **DOES NOT SUPPORT the `:allow_nil` option**. By default, Ecto validations only run if a change for the given field exists and the change value is not nil, so such as option is never needed
- You **must** use `Ecto.Changeset.get_field(changeset, :field)` to access changeset fields
- Fields which are set programmatically, such as `user_id`, must not be listed in `cast` calls or similar for security purposes. Instead they must be explicitly set when creating the struct
- **Always** invoke `mix ecto.gen.migration migration_name_using_underscores` when generating migration files, so the correct timestamp and conventions are applied
<!-- phoenix:ecto-end -->

<!-- usage-rules-end -->

Stub Stripe HTTP with `Dhc.StripeHTTPStub` (`stub/3`, `expect/4`, `form/1`, `json/3`) — no Bypass, and tests never `put_env` `:stripe_api_url`, `:stripe_secret_key` or `:stripe_req_options`. Workshop tests pick one of three seams: `Dhc.StripeHTTPStub` for a test that stubs a few Stripe routes; `DhcWeb.WorkshopStripeClient` (a whole-Stripe `Req.Test` plug, `Req.Test.stub(Dhc.Stripe, DhcWeb.WorkshopStripeClient)`) for workshop controller contract tests that should run the live adapter; and `Dhc.Workshops.StripeStub` (the `:workshop_stripe_adapter`, app-env driven) for `PaymentCommands` workflow tests whose Stripe call runs outside the test's `$callers` tree (unboxed concurrency tasks) or must be paused. The one exception: real-Stripe `:integration` suites `put_env` a real `:stripe_secret_key` and reset `:stripe_req_options` to `[]` in setup (and restore both on exit); no other test changes Stripe config. Stubs reach Tasks/inline jobs via `$callers`; other processes need `Req.Test.allow/3`. Shared subscription-payment decoding lives in `Dhc.Stripe.SubscriptionPayment` and the one retry rule in `Dhc.Stripe.Failure.retryable?/1`; see "Stubbing Stripe" in `docs/agents/notes.md`.
- Keep generated Stripe modules under `lib/dhc/stripe/generated/` excluded from Credo instead of refactoring generated source
- Use the already included and available `:req` (`Req`) library for HTTP requests, **avoid** `:httpoison`, `:tesla`, and `:httpc`. Req is included by default and is the preferred HTTP client for Phoenix apps
- **Documented exception (ADR 0021)**: transactional email goes through Swoosh, whose api client is `config :swoosh, api_client: Dhc.Email.ApiClient` wrapping `Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch` over a named `{Finch, name: Swoosh.Finch}` child in `Dhc.Application`. Finch is already a production dependency, so Hackney stays out of prod. Application code outside `Dhc.Email.*` still uses Req everywhere else.
- Hackney is test-only because Testcontainers requires its 1.x Unix-socket transport. Keep it out of production and do not force Hackney 4 until Testcontainers supports Docker Unix sockets with it; the matching Hackney advisory exceptions in `mix.exs` apply only to that test dependency.
- Nostrum's REST client pulls Gun and Cowlib into production (Gun is floored at 2.7 in `mix.exs`, which resolves Cowlib 2.21 — fixed for CVE-2026-43971 and CVE-2026-43969). Limit Cowlib advisory exceptions to explicitly reviewed CVE IDs and document the relevant exposure or mitigation in `mix.exs`; keep ignoring CVE-2026-43966 only until a fixed Cowlib release ships, and keep the Hackney 4-only CVE exceptions (CVE-2026-47069/47071/47075/47076) only while Testcontainers requires Hackney 1.x.

### Phoenix v1.8 guidelines

- **Always** begin your LiveView templates with `<Layouts.app flash={@flash} ...>` which wraps all inner content
- The `MyAppWeb.Layouts` module is aliased in the `my_app_web.ex` file, so you can use it without needing to alias it again
- Anytime you run into errors with no `current_scope` assign:
  - You failed to follow the Authenticated Routes guidelines, or you failed to pass `current_scope` to `<Layouts.app>`
  - **Always** fix the `current_scope` error by moving your routes to the proper `live_session` and ensure you pass `current_scope` as needed
- Phoenix v1.8 moved the `<.flash_group>` component to the `Layouts` module. You are **forbidden** from calling `<.flash_group>` outside of the `layouts.ex` module
- Out of the box, `core_components.ex` imports an `<.icon name="hero-x-mark" class="w-5 h-5"/>` component for hero icons. **Always** use the `<.icon>` component for icons, **never** use `Heroicons` modules or similar
- **Always** use the imported `<.input>` component for form inputs from `core_components.ex` when available. `<.input>` is imported and using it will save steps and prevent errors
- If you override the default input classes (`<.input class="myclass px-2 py-1 rounded-lg">)`) class with your own values, no default classes are inherited, so your
custom classes must fully style the input


<!-- usage-rules-start -->

<!-- phoenix:elixir-start -->
## Elixir guidelines

- Elixir lists **do not support index based access via the access syntax**

  **Never do this (invalid)**:

      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      mylist[i]

  Instead, **always** use `Enum.at`, pattern matching, or `List` for index based list access, ie:

      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      Enum.at(mylist, i)

- Elixir variables are immutable, but can be rebound, so for block expressions like `if`, `case`, `cond`, etc
  you *must* bind the result of the expression to a variable if you want to use it and you CANNOT rebind the result inside the expression, ie:

      # INVALID: we are rebinding inside the `if` and the result never gets assigned
      if connected?(socket) do
        socket = assign(socket, :val, val)
      end

      # VALID: we rebind the result of the `if` to a new variable
      socket =
        if connected?(socket) do
          assign(socket, :val, val)
        end

- **Never** nest multiple modules in the same file as it can cause cyclic dependencies and compilation errors
- **Never** use map access syntax (`changeset[:field]`) on structs as they do not implement the Access behaviour by default. For regular structs, you **must** access the fields directly, such as `my_struct.field` or use higher level APIs that are available on the struct if they exist, `Ecto.Changeset.get_field/2` for changesets
- Elixir's standard library has everything necessary for date and time manipulation. Familiarize yourself with the common `Time`, `Date`, `DateTime`, and `Calendar` interfaces by accessing their documentation as necessary. The one sanctioned date/time dependency is `tz`, the IANA database behind `Dhc.ClubCalendar`'s Europe/Dublin conversions. **Never** install additional dependencies unless asked or for date/time parsing (which you can use the `date_time_parser` package)
- Don't use `String.to_atom/1` on user input (memory leak risk)
- Predicate function names should not start with `is_` and should end in a question mark. Names like `is_thing` should be reserved for guards
- Elixir's builtin OTP primitives like `DynamicSupervisor` and `Registry`, require names in the child spec, such as `{DynamicSupervisor, name: MyApp.MyDynamicSup}`, then you can use `DynamicSupervisor.start_child(MyApp.MyDynamicSup, child_spec)`
- Use `Task.async_stream(collection, callback, options)` for concurrent enumeration with back-pressure. The majority of times you will want to pass `timeout: :infinity` as option

## Mix guidelines

- Read the docs and options before using tasks (by using `mix help task_name`)
- To debug test failures, run tests in a specific file with `mix test test/my_test.exs` or run all previously failed tests with `mix test --failed`
- `mix deps.clean --all` is **almost never needed**. **Avoid** using it unless you have good reason

## Test guidelines

- **Always use `start_supervised!/1`** to start processes in tests as it guarantees cleanup between tests
- **Avoid** `Process.sleep/1` and `Process.alive?/1` in tests
  - Instead of sleeping to wait for a process to finish, **always** use `Process.monitor/1` and assert on the DOWN message:

      ref = Process.monitor(pid)
      assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :normal}

   - Instead of sleeping to synchronize before the next call, **always** use `_ = :sys.get_state/1` to ensure the process has handled prior messages
<!-- phoenix:elixir-end -->

<!-- phoenix:phoenix-start -->
## Phoenix guidelines

- Remember Phoenix router `scope` blocks include an optional alias which is prefixed for all routes within the scope. **Always** be mindful of this when creating routes within a scope to avoid duplicate module prefixes.

- You **never** need to create your own `alias` for route definitions! The `scope` provides the alias, ie:

      scope "/admin", AppWeb.Admin do
        pipe_through :browser

        live "/users", UserLive, :index
      end

  the UserLive route would point to the `AppWeb.Admin.UserLive` module

- `Phoenix.View` no longer is needed or included with Phoenix, don't use it
<!-- phoenix:phoenix-end -->

<!-- phoenix:ecto-start -->
## Ecto Guidelines

- **Always** preload Ecto associations in queries when they'll be accessed in templates, ie a message that needs to reference the `message.user.email`
- Remember `import Ecto.Query` and other supporting modules when you write `seeds.exs`
- `Ecto.Schema` fields always use the `:string` type, even for `:text`, columns, ie: `field :name, :string`
- `Ecto.Changeset.validate_number/2` **DOES NOT SUPPORT the `:allow_nil` option**. By default, Ecto validations only run if a change for the given field exists and the change value is not nil, so such as option is never needed
- You **must** use `Ecto.Changeset.get_field(changeset, :field)` to access changeset fields
- Fields which are set programmatically, such as `user_id`, must not be listed in `cast` calls or similar for security purposes. Instead they must be explicitly set when creating the struct
- **Always** invoke `mix ecto.gen.migration migration_name_using_underscores` when generating migration files, so the correct timestamp and conventions are applied
<!-- phoenix:ecto-end -->

<!-- usage-rules-end -->

3:   Oban worker that processes bulk member invitations.
4: 
5:   Migrates the `bulk_invite_with_subscription` Deno edge function into the
6:   Phoenix/Oban runtime. The Phoenix API layer is responsible for authorising
7:   admin-level access before enqueueing this worker.
8: 
9:   ## ALE-162 — issue time is side-effect free
10: 
11:   ADR 0010 fixes that the Authentication Principal is born inside Invitation
12:   Acceptance, not at issue. This worker now performs **only** the issue-time
13:   work for each invite:
14: 
15:     * mint a fresh Phoenix UUID for `invitation.prospective_principal_id` (the eventual
16:       Principal id);
17:     * insert the pending `invitations` row carrying `email`, `date_of_birth`,
18:       `expires_at` (7 days), `created_by_principal_id`, and `invitation_type`;
19:     * enqueue the `inviteMember` email;
20:     * if the invite came from a waitlist, mark the waitlist entry `invited`.
21: 
22:   It no longer calls the Supabase admin API, creates a Stripe customer, or
23:   inserts a `user_profiles` row. Principal, profile, and Membership
24:   creation happen during acceptance. The previous per-invite Supabase-Auth /
25:   Stripe / profile-creation failure modes no longer exist at issue time; the
26:   remaining failure modes are DB insert errors and email-enqueue errors.
27: 
28:   ## Job args
29: 
30:     * `invites` — list of invite maps. Invite maps require `firstName`,
31:       `lastName`, `email`, `phoneNumber`, and `dateOfBirth`.
32:     * `user` — admin context map containing `id` and optionally `email`.
33: 
34:   The worker intentionally records per-invite failures and continues processing
35:   the rest of the batch. It only returns an error for invalid job args or an
36:   unrecoverable failure while issuing an Invitation. Batch summary failures
37:   are logged but do not fail this job, so completed per-Invitation work is
38:   never replayed.
39:   """
40: 
41:   use Oban.Worker, queue: :invitations, max_attempts: 3
42: 
43:   require Logger
44: 
45:   alias Dhc.Invitations.Repository
46:   alias Dhc.Onboarding
47:   alias Dhc.Repo
48: 
49:   @impl Worker
50:   def backoff(%Oban.Job{attempt: attempt}), do: trunc(:math.pow(attempt, 4) + 15)
51: 
52:   @impl Worker
53:   def perform(%Oban.Job{args: args} = job) do
54:     ctx = job_log_context(job)
55: 
56:     with :ok <- validate_args(args),
57:          {:ok, results} <- process_invites(args, ctx) do
58:       Logger.info(
59:         "[bulk-invite-worker] Completed bulk invitation batch",
60:         Keyword.merge(ctx,
61:           created_by: get_in(args, ["user", "id"]),
62:           total_count: length(results),
63:           success_count: Enum.count(results, & &1.success),
64:           failure_count: Enum.count(results, &(not &1.success))
65:         )
66:       )
67: 
68:       :ok
69:     else
70:       {:error, reason} = error ->
71:         # Pass the reason as a structured keyword -> string map so Sentry's PII
72:         # filter doesn't strip it (inspect/1 on error tuples can contain email
73:         # addresses, which triggers the [Filtered] redaction in Sentry's UI).
74:         reason_map = reason_to_map(reason)
75: 
76:         Sentry.capture_message("Bulk invite worker failed",
77:           level: :error,
78:           extra: %{
79:             reason: reason_map,
80:             created_by: get_in(args, ["user", "id"]),
81:             oban_job_id: ctx[:oban_job_id],
82:             oban_attempt: ctx[:oban_attempt],
83:             oban_queue: ctx[:oban_queue],
84:             oban_worker: ctx[:oban_worker]
85:           }
86:         )
87: 
88:         Logger.error(
89:           "[bulk-invite-worker] Job failed: #{inspect(reason)}",
90:           Keyword.merge(ctx,
91:             created_by: get_in(args, ["user", "id"]),
92:             reason: format_reason(reason)
93:           )
94:         )
95: 
96:         error
97:     end
98:   end
99: 
100:   defp validate_args(args) do
101:     errors =
102:       []
103:       |> validate_required(args, "invites")
104:       |> validate_invites(args)
105:       |> validate_required(args, "user")
106:       |> validate_user(args)
107: 
108:     case errors do
109:       [] -> :ok
110:       errors -> {:error, {:validation, Enum.reverse(errors)}}
111:     end
112:   end
113: 
114:   defp validate_required(errors, args, field) do
115:     if is_nil(args[field]) or args[field] == "", do: ["missing #{field}" | errors], else: errors
116:   end
117: 
118:   defp validate_invites(errors, %{"invites" => [_ | _]}),
119:     do: errors
120: 
121:   defp validate_invites(errors, %{"invites" => _invites}),
122:     do: ["invites must be a non-empty list" | errors]
123: 
124:   defp validate_invites(errors, _args), do: errors
125: 
126:   defp validate_user(errors, %{"user" => %{"id" => id}}) when is_binary(id) and id != "",
127:     do: errors
128: 
129:   defp validate_user(errors, %{"user" => _user}), do: ["user.id is required" | errors]
130:   defp validate_user(errors, _args), do: errors
131: 
132:   defp process_invites(%{"invites" => invites, "user" => %{"id" => created_by_id}}, ctx) do
133:     start_time = System.monotonic_time(:millisecond)
134: 
135:     results =
136:       invites
137:       |> Enum.with_index()
138:       |> Enum.map(fn {invite, index} -> process_one_invite(invite, index, created_by_id, ctx) end)
139: 
140:     finalize_batch(results, created_by_id, ctx)
141: 
142:     processing_time_ms = System.monotonic_time(:millisecond) - start_time
143: 
144:     Logger.info(
145:       "[bulk-invite-worker] Stored invitation processing results",
146:       Keyword.merge(ctx,
147:         created_by: created_by_id,
148:         processing_time_ms: processing_time_ms
149:       )
150:     )
151: 
152:     {:ok, results}
153:   end
154: 
155:   # Each invite already wrote its own processing-log entry (issued through
156:   # `Dhc.Onboarding.issue_invitation/3`, or refused through
157:   # `record_refused_invitation/3`); the batch adds only the summary
158:   # Notification.
159:   defp finalize_batch(results, created_by_id, ctx) do
160:     case Repository.create_processing_notification(results, created_by_id) do
161:       :ok ->
162:         :ok
163: 
164:       {:error, reason} ->
165:         Logger.error(
166:           "[bulk-invite-worker] Batch finalization failed after invitation issue completed",
167:           Keyword.merge(ctx, created_by: created_by_id, reason: format_reason(reason))
168:         )
169: 
170:         :ok
171:     end
172:   end
173: 
174:   defp process_one_invite(invite, index, created_by_id, ctx) do
175:     with {:ok, invite_data} <- invite_shape(invite),
176:          invite_data <- put_issue_key(invite_data, issue_key(ctx, index)),
177:          {:ok, result} <- issue(invite_data, created_by_id, ctx) do
178:       result
179:     else
180:       {:error, reason} ->
181:         email = invite_email(invite)
182:         reason_map = reason_to_map(reason)
183: 
184:         record_refusal(email, reason, created_by_id, ctx)
185: 
186:         Sentry.capture_message("Bulk invitation failed",
187:           level: :error,
188:           extra: %{
189:             reason: reason_map,
190:             invite_email: email,
191:             oban_job_id: ctx[:oban_job_id],
192:             oban_attempt: ctx[:oban_attempt],
193:             oban_queue: ctx[:oban_queue],
194:             oban_worker: ctx[:oban_worker]
195:           }
196:         )
197: 
198:         Logger.error(
199:           "[bulk-invite-worker] Failed to process invitation",
200:           Keyword.merge(ctx, email: email, reason: format_reason(reason))
201:         )
202: 
203:         %{email: email || "unknown", success: false, error: inspect(reason)}
204:     end
205:   end
206: 
207:   # Direct Invitations only: a Waitlist entry id is no longer an invite
208:   # (ALE-376); Waitlist people are invited from their Intake.
209:   defp invite_shape(invite) when is_map(invite), do: {:ok, invite}
210:   defp invite_shape(_invite), do: {:error, :invalid_invite_shape}
211: 
212:   defp issue(invite_data, created_by_id, ctx) do
213:     issue_key = get_in(invite_data, ["metadata", "issue_key"])
214: 
215:     case Repository.invitation_id_for_issue_key(issue_key) do
216:       {:ok, invitation_id} ->
217:         {:ok, invitation_result(invite_data["email"], invitation_id)}
218: 
219:       :not_found ->
220:         Repo.transaction(fn -> issue_in_transaction(invite_data, created_by_id, ctx) end)
221:     end
222:   end
223: 
224:   defp issue_in_transaction(invite_data, created_by_id, ctx) do
225:     case Onboarding.issue_invitation(invite_data, created_by_id) do
226:       {:ok, %{invitation_id: invitation_id, email: email}} ->
227:         Logger.info(
228:           "[bulk-invite-worker] Processed invitation",
229:           Keyword.merge(ctx, email: email, invitation_id: invitation_id)
230:         )
231: 
232:         invitation_result(email, invitation_id)
233: 
234:       {:error, reason} ->
235:         Repo.rollback(reason)
236:     end
237:   end
238: 
239:   defp record_refusal(email, reason, created_by_id, ctx) do
240:     case Onboarding.record_refused_invitation(email, reason, created_by_id) do
241:       :ok ->
242:         :ok
243: 
244:       {:error, log_reason} ->
245:         Logger.error(
246:           "[bulk-invite-worker] Failed to record a refused invitation",
247:           Keyword.merge(ctx, created_by: created_by_id, reason: format_reason(log_reason))
248:         )
249:     end
250:   end
251: 
252:   defp invitation_result(email, invitation_id) do
253:     %{email: email, success: true, invitationId: invitation_id}
254:   end
255: 
256:   defp issue_key(ctx, index), do: "bulk-invite:#{ctx[:oban_job_id] || "unpersisted"}:#{index}"
257: 
258:   defp put_issue_key(invite_data, issue_key) do
259:     metadata = Map.get(invite_data, "metadata") || %{}
260:     Map.put(invite_data, "metadata", Map.put(metadata, "issue_key", issue_key))
261:   end
262: 
263:   defp invite_email(%{"email" => email}), do: email
264:   defp invite_email(_invite), do: nil
265: 
266:   defp job_log_context(%Oban.Job{} = job) do
267:     [
268:       oban_job_id: job.id,
269:       oban_attempt: job.attempt,
270:       oban_queue: job.queue,
271:       oban_worker: job.worker
272:     ]
273:   end
274: 
275:   # Convert an error reason into a plain string-keyed map so Sentry's PII
276:   # filter doesn't redact it. inspect/1 on tuples that contain emails (e.g.
277:   # {:email_enqueue, %{email: "..."}}) triggers Sentry's [Filtered] redaction.
278:   # We stringify atoms and keep values as strings; nested maps are flattened
279:   # one level. Anything we can't structurize falls back to inspect/1.
280:   defp reason_to_map(reason) when is_tuple(reason) do
281:     reason
282:     |> Tuple.to_list()
283:     |> Enum.with_index()
284:     |> Enum.into(%{}, fn {value, idx} -> {Integer.to_string(idx), stringify(value)} end)
285:   end
286: 
287:   defp reason_to_map(reason) when is_map(reason) do
288:     Enum.into(reason, %{}, fn {k, v} -> {stringify(k), stringify(v)} end)
289:   end
290: 
291:   defp reason_to_map(reason) when is_list(reason) do
292:     Enum.into(reason, %{}, fn v -> {stringify(v), true} end)
293:   end
294: 
295:   defp reason_to_map(reason), do: %{"value" => stringify(reason)}
296: 
297:   defp stringify(value) when is_binary(value), do: value
298:   defp stringify(value) when is_atom(value), do: Atom.to_string(value)
299:   defp stringify(value) when is_number(value), do: to_string(value)
300:   defp stringify(value), do: inspect(value)
301: 
302:   defp format_reason(reason) when is_binary(reason), do: reason
303:   defp format_reason({:validation, errors}), do: "validation: #{Enum.join(errors, ", ")}"
304:   defp format_reason(other), do: inspect(other)
305: end

No test asserts resend expiry. So the only "1 day" is the resend re-arm.

Plan: Introduce a single owner for invitation validity: `Dhc.Invitations.Validity` with `default_days/0` = 7, `expires_at/1` (from a now). Use it in:
- `Repository.insert_pending_invitation` (replacing the inline 7)
- `Invitations.refresh_for_resend` (replacing 1 day → 7 days)

Wait — is changing resend from 1 day to 7 days what the user wants? "make the default invitation validity to be 7 days". The default validity of an invitation. Issue time already is 7. The resend one is a "fresh short expiry window" of 1 day — which is arguably a bug: a resent invitation only lives 1 day while a fresh one lives 7. Consistency argues for 7.

But careful: maybe the user believes the default is currently something else (e.g., they saw 1 day somewhere). Either way, making it consistently 7 days across both paths satisfies the request.

Should it be configurable? A config-driven value would be nicer: `config :dhc, :invitation_validity_days, 7`. Hmm, the AGENTS guidance says minimal complete change. Let me check if config has a pattern for such things. I think a simple module attribute with 7 days in one owner module is good; adding config is optional. I'll add a config-backed value with default 7 — actually that adds runtime surface (runtime.exs maybe). Keep simpler: module attribute default 7 days in `Dhc.Invitations.Validity`.

Hmm, but is there any repo convention like "one place owns X"? Yes, AGENTS.md is heavy on that: "Billing days have one owner". So creating `Dhc.Invitations.Validity` with `days/0` and `expires_at/1` fits well.

Also check the frontend — is there any place where invitation validity is displayed/assumed (e.g., "your invitation expires in X")? The pricing/acceptance side uses `expires_at` from the invitation. Also `Dhc.Onboarding.Acceptance` uses session expiry min with invitation expiry. Not needed.

Also check the "beginners workshop invite" handoff path — it uses `issue_invitation/3` → Repository → 7 days. Good.

Also the bulk invite worker — does it insert invitations itself with a different expiry? It mentions expires_at (7 days) in a doc comment. Let me check it.

defmodule Dhc.Invitations.Validity do
  @moduledoc """
  The one owner of how long an Invitation stays valid.

  Every place that stamps `invitations.expires_at` — issuing a fresh
  Invitation and re-arming one on resend — reads its window from here, so the
  validity a member sees is the same on both paths. The invite email template
  (`packages/email-templates/emails/invite-member.tsx`) states the same number
  in its copy; change both together.

  The window is configurable with `:invitation_validity_days` (see
  `config/config.exs`); a missing or invalid value falls back to the seven-day
  default.
  """

  @default_validity_days 7

  @spec days() :: pos_integer()
  def days do
    case Application.get_env(:dhc, :invitation_validity_days, @default_validity_days) do
      days when is_integer(days) and days > 0 -> days
      _other -> @default_validity_days
    end
  end

  @spec expires_at(DateTime.t()) :: DateTime.t()
  def expires_at(now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    now |> DateTime.add(days(), :day) |> DateTime.truncate(:second)
  end
end

defmodule Dhc.Invitations.Validity do
  @moduledoc """
  The one owner of how long an Invitation stays valid.

  Every place that stamps `invitations.expires_at` — issuing a fresh
  Invitation (`Dhc.Invitations.Repository.insert_pending_invitation/3`) and
  re-arming one on resend (`Dhc.Invitations`) — reads its window from here, so
  the validity a member gets is the same on both paths.

  The window is configurable with `:invitation_validity_days` (see
  `config/config.exs`); a missing or invalid value falls back to the seven-day
  default. The invite email copy in
  `packages/email-templates/emails/invite-member.tsx` states the same number —
  change both together.
  """

  @default_validity_days 7

  @doc """
  How many days an Invitation stays valid from the moment it is issued or
  re-armed.
  """
  @spec days() :: pos_integer()
  def days do
    case Application.get_env(:dhc, :invitation_validity_days, @default_validity_days) do
      days when is_integer(days) and days > 0 -> days
      _other -> @default_validity_days
    end
  end

  @doc """
  The instant an Invitation issued (or re-armed) at `now` expires.
  """
  @spec expires_at(DateTime.t()) :: DateTime.t()
  def expires_at(now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    now
    |> DateTime.add(days(), :day)
    |> DateTime.truncate(:second)
  end
end

defmodule Dhc.Invitations.ValidityTest do
  use Dhc.DataCase, async: false

  alias Dhc.AuthFixtures
  alias Dhc.Invitations
  alias Dhc.Invitations.Invitation
  alias Dhc.Invitations.Validity
  alias Dhc.Onboarding

  describe "days/0" do
    test "defaults to seven days" do
      assert Validity.days() == 7
    end

    test "honours the configured window" do
      put_validity_days(14)
      assert Validity.days() == 14
    end

    test "falls back to the default for a window that is not a positive number of days" do
      put_validity_days(0)
      assert Validity.days() == 7

      put_validity_days("14")
      assert Validity.days() == 7
    end
  end

  describe "expires_at/1" do
    test "adds the validity window to the given instant" do
      assert Validity.expires_at(~U[2026-11-10 09:00:00Z]) == ~U[2026-11-17 09:00:00Z]
    end

    test "follows the configured window" do
      put_validity_days(14)
      assert Validity.expires_at(~U[2026-11-10 09:00:00Z]) == ~U[2026-11-24 09:00:00Z]
    end
  end

  describe "the Invitation rows" do
    test "a newly issued invitation is valid for the default window" do
      {invitation, admin} = issue_invitation()

      assert DateTime.diff(invitation.expires_at, DateTime.utc_now(), :hour) in 167..169

      _ = admin
    end

    test "a resent invitation is re-armed with the same window" do
      {invitation, admin} = issue_invitation()

      Repo.update_all(from(i in Invitation, where: i.id == ^invitation.id),
        set: [status: "expired"]
      )

      before = DateTime.utc_now()

      assert {:ok, %{succeeded: 1, failed: 0}} =
               Invitations.resend_invitation_emails([invitation.email], admin.id)

      rearmed = Repo.get!(Invitation, invitation.id)
      assert rearmed.status == "pending"
      assert DateTime.diff(rearmed.expires_at, before, :hour) in 167..169
    end
  end

  defp put_validity_days(days) do
    Application.put_env(:dhc, :invitation_validity_days, days)
    on_exit(fn -> Application.put_env(:dhc, :invitation_validity_days, 7) end)
  end

  defp issue_invitation do
    admin = AuthFixtures.principal_fixture()
    email = "validity-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"

    invite = %{
      "firstName" => "Ada",
      "lastName" => "Lovelace",
      "email" => email,
      "phoneNumber" => "+353871234567",
      "dateOfBirth" => "1990-01-01"
    }

    {:ok, %{invitation_id: invitation_id}} =
      Repo.transaction(fn ->
        case Onboarding.issue_invitation(invite, admin.id) do
          {:ok, result} -> result
          {:error, reason} -> Repo.rollback(reason)
        end
      end)

    {Repo.get!(Invitation, invitation_id), admin}
  end
end

docs/agents/where-to-look.md:39:| Send an attended person their Invitation (the Invitation handoff), change the Invitable view, or what deleting an Invitation does to a standing | `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/beginners_workshops/commands/attendance.ex` (`invite` run clause, `invite_locked/3`, `invite_details/1`, `record_invite_refusal/2`) + `invitable.ex` (the cross-workshop read model) + `workshop_console.ex` (roster `standing`, `finalisation.invitations`) + `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/invitations.ex` (`delete_many/1`, `delete_and_restore_standing/1`) + `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/auth/capabilities.ex` (`members.invite` includes `beginners_coordinator`) + `dhc_web/controllers/beginners_workshop_invitations_{controller,json}.ex` (slice `beginnersWorkshopInvitations`: `GET /api/beginners-workshops/invitable`, `POST /:id/intakes/:intakeId/invite`, pipeline `:members_invite`) + `apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/beginners-workshop/` (`invitations.remote.ts`, `invite-button.svelte`, `invitable-tab.svelte`, the Invitable tab in `+page.svelte`/`+page.server.ts`) + `workshops/[workshopId]/workshop-console.svelte` (Invite per attended row, `canInvite`) + `lib/beginners-workshops/console.ts` (`invitationSummary`, `standingLabel`, `followUpLabel`); tests `test/dhc/beginners_workshops/invitation_handoff_test.exs`, `beginners_workshop_invitations_controller_test.exs`, `beginners_workshops_client_parity_test.exs`, `capabilities_test.exs`, `invitable-tab.browser.test.ts`, `workshop-console.browser.test.ts`, `console.test.ts` | ALE-392. `{:invite, workshop_id, intake_id}` (`members.invite`) locks Beginners' Workshop → the Intake's Waitlist entry → the Intake and refuses `:not_finalised`, `:not_attended`, `:already_invited` / `:already_joined` / `:not_invitable` (standing), `:person_not_found` (anonymised); the Follow-up never gates it. It then calls `Dhc.Onboarding.issue_invitation/3` with `waitlist_id:` (standard tier, 7 days, `invitationType` `beginners_workshop`) and `Waitlist.change_standing(id, "invited")` in the same transaction. Onboarding's refusals map to `:email_is_principal`, `:email_has_pending_invitation`, `:incomplete_details` (422) and anything else (the pending-email index race) to `:concurrent_change`; they are logged with `record_refused_invitation/3` after the rollback. Deleting Invitations locks the affected Waitlist entries **before** deleting (entry → Invitation, the order `invite` takes) and moves each `invited` entry with no remaining pending/expired Invitation back to `attended`; Onboarding never calls into Beginners' Workshops. The Invitable view lists standing `attended` people with their latest attended Intake in a finalised workshop (oldest workshop first) and the Follow-up as `sent` (log `queued_at`) or `scheduled` (`WorkshopPolicy.follow_up_at/1`). Acceptance is unchanged (`invited → joined`, claims the Waitlist profile and Guardian only through `waitlist_id`, never by email). Resend re-arms an expired Invitation only if `Dhc.Invitations.EmailRefusals.invitable/3` still allows it (`resend_invitation_emails/2` logs each refusal under the resending Principal). |

docs/adr/0014-verified-discord-continuation-in-invitation-acceptance.md:20:The credential-verification proof remains a 15-minute Phoenix token as in ADR-0010. Redeeming it creates or resumes the Invitation's one active Attempt and creates a fresh `awaiting_oauth` Continuation. The Continuation expires at the earlier of 15 minutes after creation and the Invitation's normal expiry. Re-verifying credentials before either expiry may resume the same Attempt but must create a new Continuation after an expired, cancelled, or failed one; it must not extend a live Continuation. The browser receives only the opaque Continuation identifier in its protected Phoenix session. It is not placed in a URL, OAuth `state`, client-side storage, or a signed bearer token.
docs/adr/0014-verified-discord-continuation-in-invitation-acceptance.md:22:Starting OAuth records the Continuation identifier next to Assent's per-browser state and PKCE session parameters. The OAuth callback must restore and validate those parameters, load the same `awaiting_oauth` Continuation, and require that its Invitation and Attempt are still current. A missing or replaced browser session, invalid OAuth state, PKCE failure, provider error, or expired Continuation completes no verification and makes no Stripe mutation; the prospective Member restarts OAuth through the same Attempt after again proving Invitation credentials if necessary. The callback uses only Assent's normalized `sub` as the provider subject and treats `preferred_username` and all other claims as mutable metadata.
docs/adr/0014-verified-discord-continuation-in-invitation-acceptance.md:24:On a successful callback, one short database transaction locks the Invitation, Attempt, and Continuation; rechecks all expiry and status fences; and changes the Continuation to `verified`. It also creates an **active Discord subject claim** for `(discord, sub)`. 40:| Run a console Intake command (decline, resend/rotate link), change `availableCommands`, the Intake history or the console Intake detail | `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/beginners_workshops/commands/intake_commands.ex` (`intake_command/6`, `act_on_intake/4`; the link email is `IntakeEmails.deliver/5` with `:link`) + `intake_policy.ex` (the one rule: `check/2`, `available_commands/1`, over the closed facts `facts/1` builds for both adapters; `legacy_facts/1` only reads the pre-ALE-402 partial maps of old direct tests) + `intake_event.ex` (history schema, `beginners_workshop_intake_events`) + `workshop_console.ex` (roster `medical`, `link_generation`, `window_ends_at`, `email_log`, `history`, `available_commands`; `unpaid_after_window`) + `dhc_web/controllers/beginners_workshop_intakes_{controller,json}.ex` (slice `beginnersWorkshopIntakes`: `POST /:id/intakes/:intakeId/decline \| resend-link \| rotate-link`) + `apps/web/src/routes/dashboard/beginners-workshop/workshops/[workshopId]/intake-detail.svelte` (the roster row's sheet) + `console.remote.ts` (`runIntakeCommand`) + `lib/schemas/beginnersWorkshop.ts` (`intakeCommandSchema`) + `lib/beginners-workshops/console.ts` (`INTAKE_COMMANDS`, `intakeCommandLabel`, `emailLogLine`, `historyLine`, `unpaidAfterWindowText`); tests `test/dhc/beginners_workshops/intake_commands{,_concurrency}_test.exs`, `beginners_workshop_intakes_controller_test.exs`, `workshop-console.browser.test.ts` | ALE-386. See the Waitlist registration row in `docs/agents/where-to-look.md`.
 
 Member Announcements (ADR 0028) are committee emails to all members, BCC'd and sent through Resend's batch API as inline HTML. They are deliberately not Email Kinds: React Email generates gitignored `apps/phoenix/priv/email_shells/` artifacts before Phoenix compilation. Phoenix mise tasks and CI generate automatically; direct Mix/Docker builds need `mise run email-shells` first. Fly deployment generates on the runner before uploading the Docker context, so keep the artifacts out of `.dockerignore`. The body is a Tiptap JSON document that Phoenix renders from a closed vocabulary, and the live preview is Phoenix's render. See the Member Announcement row in `docs/agents/where-to-look.md`.

Queueing never refuses a template that passed the save-time measure: if HTML escaping pushes the filled body over 2,000 characters, each value is shortened until its escaped form fits its placeholder maximum. The 2,000-character measure must keep matching `packages/email-templates/fixtures/intake-email-measure.json`, which the dashboard counter shares. See the Intake Email row in `docs/agents/where-to-look.md`.

The existing tests explicitly assert the 1-day resend window ("The resend refreshed the expiry window from +7 days to +1 day."). So the 1-day re-arm was a deliberate design decision, not a bug. Changing it is a behaviour change beyond "make the default invitation validity 7 days".

Hmm. Now the question: what does the user actually want? "make the default invitation validity to be 7 days". The issue path was already 7 days. So the only thing to change to satisfy "default validity is 7 days" is... nothing? Unless they mean the resend's 1-day window should also be 7.

Interpretation options:
A. The default validity (issue path) = 7 days: already true; nothing to do (but then the request is moot).
B. Make validity uniform at 7 days, including resend re-arm: what I did.

Given the request, B is the sensible read: the user wants invitations to be valid 7 days (maybe they observed 1 day somewhere, e.g. after a resend, or maybe they just want it set explicitly).

But B conflicts with an existing deliberate test. Changing an existing test to match new behaviour is acceptable when the behaviour change is intended. The user asked for 7-day default validity; the 1-day resend window is exactly the thing that makes validity not 7 days. I'll go with B and update those two tests, keeping their intent (the resend refreshes the expiry; the expired sibling is untouched).

But wait — there's a subtlety in test 1: `assert refreshed.expires_at != original.expires_at`. With the same 7-day window and an immediate resend, they're equal (same second). The test's intent — "refreshes expiry" — is now only observable when the invitation was issued earlier. I should update the test to reflect the new behaviour meaningfully: e.g. insert an invitation with an already-near expiry (seconds: -something) and assert the resend sets it to now + 7 days. Let me look at `insert_invitation` helper to see the `seconds` param semantics.

Now update the two failing tests to encode the new behaviour:

Test 1 (line 513): "resending a real pending invitation refreshes expiry and enqueues an email". New expectation: the re-armed expiry is the default validity window from the resend moment (now + 7 days). To keep "refreshes expiry" meaningful, insert the invitation with `seconds: -3600` (created an hour ago → original expires_at = created+7d = now+7d-1h), then after resend expires_at should be now+7d (different from original, and equals now + 7 days).

Let me rewrite:

```elixir
      email = "real@example.com"
      ...
      # Issued an hour ago, so its window ends an hour before a fresh one.
      invitation_id = insert_invitation(email: email, status: "pending", seconds: -3600)
      original = Repo.get(Invitation, invitation_id)
      ...
      # The resend re-arms the invitation with the default validity window.
      refreshed = Repo.get(Invitation, invitation_id)
      assert refreshed.expires_at != original.expires_at

      expected = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), 7, :day) |> DateTime.truncate(:second)
      assert DateTime.diff(refreshed.expires_at, expected, :second) in -5..5
```

Careful with `DateTime.diff` sign: diff(refreshed, expected, :second) in -5..5 works either way.

Test 2 (line 586): update expected from 1 day to 7 days.

Better: reference `Dhc.Invitations.Validity.expires_at/1` for the expectation so the test doesn't hardcode 7? The test file is a controller test; using the owner module is cleaner:

```elixir
expected = Dhc.Invitations.Validity.expires_at()
assert DateTime.diff(refreshed.expires_at, expected, :second) in -5..5
```
But that makes the test tautological (it would pass with any window). The controller test should assert the literal 7-day window; the Validity unit test asserts days() == 7. I'll use the literal 7 days in the controller test to keep it a real check.
